_README: ChArUco board definition for calibration/charuco_calibrate.py (PHASE 5).
square_length_m and marker_length_m are PHYSICAL LENGTHS OF THE BOARD AS
YOU ACTUALLY DISPLAY IT. They are not derived from anything and nothing
in this repository knows them -- you must measure them.
* Printed on paper: measure the printed square with a ruler.
* Shown on a monitor: measure the square ON THE SCREEN. Do NOT compute
it from the panel's spec sheet, and do not trust the OS's reported
DPI -- scaling settings make both unreliable.
Measure across as many squares as you can and divide, e.g. span 6
squares, measure 180.0 mm, square_length_m = 0.180 / 6 = 0.030.
WHAT THESE NUMBERS AFFECT
fx, fy, cx, cy and the distortion coefficients are in PIXELS and are
unaffected by a scale error. Every metric quantity that follows -- board
pose, hand-eye translation, and eventually reconstruction scale -- is
linearly wrong by the same factor. A 2% error in square_length_m is a 2%
error in every distance you ever compute from this camera.
Set "measured": true once you have measured them, so the tools stop
warning. The values below are PLACEHOLDER DEFAULTS.
To generate a board image to print or display:
python calibration/charuco_capture.py --generate-board board.png
then measure it and come back here.
note: Measured 2026-08-19 on the portable laptop. Board rendered at 200 px/square (calibration/data/board/charuco_7x5_200px.png, 1440x1040) and displayed at 100% zoom; the FULL 7-square width was measured as 212.8 mm and divided, giving 30.4 mm per square (30.4 x 30.4 -- squares confirmed square, which is also a check that the viewer is not stretching the image). Implied display density 167.1 DPI, agreeing with a 13.3-inch 1920x1080 panel (165.6 DPI) to 0.9% -- independent evidence the image is not being rescaled by the viewer. *** FILL IN THE ACTUAL MACHINE/PANEL HERE. *** Spanning 7 squares makes a +/-0.5 mm reading a 0.23% scale error rather than the 1.6% a single square would give. IF THE DISPLAY, MACHINE OR ZOOM CHANGES, THIS MUST BE RE-MEASURED: every distance the rig reports scales linearly with it, and the error is invisible in fx/fy/cx/cy and in every reprojection residual.
